The *Chakkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.6) is the sixth section of the main exposition of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the book of personal designations in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Following the analytical scheme of the text, this chapter sets out designations and definitions of individuals grouped into sets of six, providing the detailed doctrinal definitions corresponding to the summary headings established in the *Chakkauddesa* (Pp 1.6) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists two translations of the text across two languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse data from DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing of material across the Pali canon, identifying 264 matching passages across 23 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual overlaps occur with the *Dasakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 10), the *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), and the introductory summary matrix in the *Chakkauddesa* (Pp 1.6) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with other chapters of the *Puggalapaññatti* (such as Pp 2.1 and Pp 2.9), the *Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta* (MN 9), the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 21 and Cnd 22), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.3), and later commentary and sub-commentary literature [DharmaNexus]. No significant cross-language alignments with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora are recorded in the automated match data [DharmaNexus].
